top_choice_rationale: The experimental discovery of the Higgs boson by two independent detectors is the most consequential unrecognised experimental result on the shortlist, mature after more than a decade of mass, spin-parity and coupling measurements. P002 (Gianotti, Jenni, Virdee) carries each detector from conception through construction to operation, with Gianotti and Jenni common to every Higgs proposal. P003 differs only in putting Della Negra in the CMS seat, so it ranks second. P001 (Katori and Ye) has the cleanest attribution and a mature, reproduced result, but is narrower in significance and overlaps the 2005 and 2012 metrology prizes, so it is my fallback and still ranks above no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; Chalmers colleagues of the 2025 laureates are not candidates here, and no listed connection to Higgs or lattice-clock candidates
